$comment: THE list of API keys the board knows about — read by the server (server/secrets.mjs: only these names can be saved), the board's API keys dialog (src/lib/apiKeys.ts) and tests/test_api_keys.py (every key must be read by something). Values are stored beside it in setup/.env (git-ignored, docker-ignored, never served). Each key has a kind: secret (masked; the default), url (shown in full; a new URL clears its service's secrets), email or text (shown in full). 'planned: true' marks a key the user can add now that nothing reads yet; tests/test_api_keys.py exempts only those.

services.name: Jira
services.why: Pulls every ticket on the board. Without it nothing can be fetched.
services.getIt: Jira → Profile → Personal Access Tokens → Create token

keys.label: Base URL
keys.hint: Leave empty to use endpoints.jiraBase from the config.

services.name: Atlassian Cloud
services.why: One API token for Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket on Atlassian Cloud, as they move off on-prem.
usedBy: Bitbucket (when no HTTP access token is set)
services.getIt: id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens → Create API token

keys.label: Account email
keys.hint: Cloud API calls sign in with this email plus the token.

services.name: Bitbucket
services.why: Adds real branches, pull requests and review state to the cards.
services.getIt: Bitbucket → Personal settings → HTTP access tokens (read scope is enough)

keys.label: Base URL
keys.hint: Leave empty to use endpoints.bitbucketBase from the config.

services.name: Confluence
services.why: Lets the agent fallback read linked Confluence pages. The normal fetch does not need it.
services.getIt: Confluence → Profile → Personal Access Tokens → Create token

keys.label: Base URL
keys.hint: Leave empty to use endpoints.confluenceBase from the config.

services.name: Jenkins
services.why: Reads the latest build of a ticket's branch per environment: result, tests, deploy target, failed stage.
services.getIt: Jenkins → your name → Configure → API Token → Add new token

keys.label: API token
keys.hint: Job links per repository and environment go in the config (jenkins.jobs).

services.name: Checkmarx One
services.why: Confirms which vulnerabilities a fix ticket actually closed, for its PR readiness report.
services.getIt: Checkmarx One → Identity and Access Management → API Keys (the Checkmarx MCP server uses the same key)

keys.label: Tenant API URL
keys.hint: e.g. https://your-tenant.cxone.cloud — or endpoints.checkmarxBase in the config.

keys.label: Token URL
keys.hint: Only when the IAM host differs from the API host.

services.name: Claude
services.why: Runs Cloud AI with Claude models, billed to this key's Anthropic account.

services.name: Cursor
services.why: Runs Cloud AI with Cursor models, and the default agent fallback when the fast fetch fails.

services.name: Gemini
services.why: Runs Cloud AI with Gemini models, billed to this key's Google account.

services.name: OpenAI
services.why: Only for the agent fallback when the codex connector is the active one.

services.name: GitHub
services.why: Not used yet — for repositories hosted on GitHub.
services.getIt: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens (fine-grained, read-only)
